comments.note: testcase/std_testcase.php's fuzz loop calls mt_rand() so its assertions were non-deterministic and could silently pass/fail depending on random output. The new StandardTest replaces this with a seeded deterministic character-cycle algorithm, making the test reproducible.

Many assertions in the original invalid_testcase.php used hardcoded \r\n line endings (Windows-style CRLF), suggesting the file was authored on Windows. This causes portability issues in cross-platform CI pipelines. Normalising line endings in test fixtures would improve portability.

testcase/std_testcase.php's 'chemistry formula' string does not round-trip: the library parses '<1 mol%' as a broken tag opener and discards trailing content. The original test's assert() silently passed because PHP assert() was not configured to throw. The PHPUnit test documents this as a known non-round-trip edge case.

The testBadHtmlDoesNotThrow test covers three malformed strings that the original source only loaded without asserting anything. The test documents the intent (no exception thrown) rather than asserting specific output, which is the correct approach for severely broken markup edge cases.

The chemistry formula test correctly documents the known non-round-trip behavior of '<1 mol%' rather than asserting round-trip equality. This is the right design choice.

summary: Code review of tests/Parsing/InvalidHtmlTest.php, StandardTest.php, and StripTest.php. All three files are well-structured, comprehensive, and demonstrate the best patterns in the suite (DataProvider, typed providers, deterministic fuzz). No blocking issues. Four low-priority observations including a cross-cutting local-$dom leak pattern now logged at project level.

comments.note: StandardTest.php: use of PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\DataProvider attribute and properly typed @return array<string, array{string}> on both provider methods is the correct PHPUnit 10+ pattern. Deterministic fuzz via ($i*7+$j*13)%$len is simple, reproducible, and removes the mt_rand() flakiness. This is the most architecturally sound implementation in the WP-005 batch.

StandardTest::testFuzzString calls $this->dom->load($str, false) instead of load($str, true, false). The $stripRN parameter defaults to true but none of the generated strings contain \r\n so there is no correctness issue. Consider aligning with the project-wide load($str, true, false) convention for consistency.

InvalidHtmlTest.php continues the recurring local-$dom pattern seen in WP-003 (ReaderElementTest) and WP-004 (ReaderSelectorTest): local vars from str_get_html() with manual clear() that can leak if an assertion fails. This is now a confirmed cross-test-suite pattern requiring a project-wide cleanup pass. Tracking in project-level comment.

StripTest::testPhpShortTags correctly uses nowdoc (<<<'HTML') to prevent PHP from interpreting the <?= and <?php sequences inside the fixture string. This is an excellent practice worth noting for future test authors writing fixtures with PHP-like content.
